text:
liz: quick brain dump from this morning's pairing about unifying the adapter surface across hosting modes. not an RFC yet, just a strawman for feedback.

omar: paste it here please. i'm tracking auth/telemetry implications.

liz: ok. strawman summary: 1) define a minimal "handshake_v1" (flat fields) exchanged at session start: handshake_version, model, seq_hint, cache_mode_hint, kernel_prefs, auth_scheme. 2) split responsibilities: Adapter-Core = pure runtime (no tenant metadata, only hints), Adapter-Orch = all routing, tenant resolution, and auth token vending. 3) introduce a translator binary (bridge-adapter) for legacy adapters that speaks old fields and emits handshake_v1. 4) explicit failure semantics: Core returns clear error codes and metrics, orch decides reroute/degrade.

kai: suggest Core never gets raw tokens. orch should hand over a short-lived credential reference, not the token itself. keep secrets out of runtime logs.

liz: agreed. we can use a grpc header with a short opaque credential id that the runtime validates with the agent-token-proxy over mTLS. no token parsing inside Core.

maria: cache behaviour: hosted uses soft-shared caches, dedicated uses tenant-namespaced caches, private sometimes needs pinned allocation. how do we avoid leaking tenancy into Core?

omar: the cache_mode_hint enum: [soft_shared, namespace_isolated, pinned]. orch maps tenant profile -> hint. Core implements semantics purely by hint. that's similar to what we discussed before but i think we should add an explicit "resource_granularity" field (per-tenant/per-model/global) for telemetry.

tanya: ops: insist that Core emits a metric when it cannot satisfy a hint (error CAPABILITY_MISMATCH) and include hint+handshake_version in the trace. orch must have fallback rules declaratively configured.

liz: fallback config sample i suggested:

```
fallbacks:
  - when: CAPABILITY_MISMATCH
    action: route_to_pool:dedicated-fallback
  - when: AUTH_REQUIRED
    action: request_agent_token
```

kai: about kernel_prefs: if orch supplies exact kernel names for perf, Core should validate and accept only if safe. otherwise return KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED. we shouldn't silently choose a different kernel. explicitness avoids sneaky perf regressions.

maria: testing: we need an adapter-fake harness that can run in CI and emulate orch+bridge+token-proxy. it should be able to flip cache_mode_hint and kernel_prefs to exercise regressions.

omar: migration cadence proposal: - week A: land handshake proto + unit tests behind feature flag - week B: publish bridge-adapter and adapter-fake in runtime CI - week C: canary on a small dedicated pool - week D: opt-in hosted customers + private partner migrations - week F: deprecate legacy adapter surface in hosted; keep bridge for private for 6+ months.

tanya: SRE runbook (short):
1) if CAPABILITY_MISMATCH rate > 0.5% for 5m -> disable handshake_flag -> switch orch to legacy routing -> page oncall if persists.
2) if AUTH_REQUIRED spikes -> enable token-proxy debug (for 15m) and capture only correlation ids, do not log tokens.

sre-bot: note: runbook attached to incident wiki at https://internal/ops/runbooks/adapter-handshake.md

kai: versioning: handshake_version must be required. only additive fields allowed in minor bumps. major bump (v2) requires bridge translation. include a "deprecated_fields" list so bridge can warn.

liz: telemetry: require these tags on every request span: handshake_version, cache_mode_hint, kernel_prefs_applied, bridge_used (bool). we can use these to roll back if SLOs regress.

omar: config snippet for bridge-adapter mapping (example):

```
bridge:
  mode: proxy
  mappings:
    legacy_cache: cache_mode_hint
    legacy_kernels: kernel_prefs
```

maria: customer note: Private installs may ask us to keep the bridge binary indefinitely. recommend we ship a compatibility patch channel for private + a deprecation notice cycle of 12 months. hosted/dedicated stricter.

liz: agreed. RFC will document separate retirement schedules by deployment type.

tanya: also add instrumentation alerts for kernel_fallbacks and cache_eviction_rate spikes during rollout. those are good early indicators of perf issues.

kai: one more: provide an "adhoc-inspect" endpoint on the bridge-adapter that returns last-handshake (no sensitive tokens) so ops can triage mismatches without jumping into logs. must be RBAC protected.

liz: thanks — i'll convert this into an RFC draft tonight. main open questions i want flagged here: longer private compatibility window (yes from maria), exact semantics for kernel acceptance (kai wants strict), and the telemetry fields list (omar/tanya).

omar: add migration telemetry to RFC. also include a sample PromQL for CAPABILITY_MISMATCH.

maria: i'll coordinate with customer success to pre-notify private customers.

tanya: i'll draft runbook snippets for the RFC.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: tracking issue created: https://internal/issue/INF-2048 (adapter-handshake-unify).

liz: perfect. thanks all, i'll ping when RFC is up.
